shocks.name: Oil price shock
shocks.text: Oil prices quadruple; the Gulf construction boom begins and mass migration of Pakistani workers follows.

shocks.name: Second oil shock
shocks.text: Iranian revolution and a second oil price jump; Soviet forces enter Afghanistan in December.

shocks.name: Oil price collapse
shocks.text: Falling oil prices squeeze Gulf wages and hiring as the first migration boom fades.

shocks.name: Gulf War
shocks.text: Iraq invades Kuwait; many Pakistani workers return home from the Gulf.

shocks.name: Nuclear tests and sanctions
shocks.text: Sanctions follow the tests and foreign-currency accounts are frozen, pushing inflows out of formal channels.

shocks.name: 9/11 and hawala crackdown
shocks.text: Tighter rules on informal money transfers move remittances back into banks.

shocks.name: Kashmir earthquake
shocks.text: Large relief inflows, including from the diaspora.

shocks.name: Global financial crisis
shocks.text: Pakistan turns to the IMF for a stand-by loan as the balance of payments comes under strain.

shocks.name: Floods
shocks.text: The worst floods in decades hit a fifth of the country.

shocks.name: Oil price slump
shocks.text: Oil falls sharply into 2016, weakening Gulf economies and hiring.

shocks.name: COVID-19
shocks.text: Lockdowns and travel stops worldwide; remittances dip, then rebound strongly.

shocks.name: Floods and political turmoil
shocks.text: Monsoon floods, a change of government and a sliding rupee.

shocks.name: Balance-of-payments crisis
shocks.text: Reserves run very low, import curbs apply and the open-market dollar rate runs well above the official rate.

shocks.name: IMF stand-by deal
shocks.text: A $3bn IMF programme restores stability; a larger programme follows in September 2024.

shocks.name: India–Pakistan conflict
shocks.text: Brief military conflict in early May.

shocks.name: War on Iran begins
shocks.text: Oil prices spike and Gulf disruption raises fears for remittances and reserves.
